(NYSE:RF) today reported third quarter 2026 earnings of $611 million and diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.71. On an adjusted basis, earnings (1) were $622 million and diluted EPS (1) was $0.73. On both a reported and adjusted basis (1) , earnings increased 11 percent and diluted EPS increased 16 percent compared to the third quarter of 2025. "At Regions Bank, we're seeing the benefits of the investments we're making in talent, technology and strategic growth. By remaining disciplined in our approach to risk management and staying committed to soundness, profitability, and growth, we are delivering strong results built on solid fundamentals and a competitive strategy. Strong credit quality, continued momentum in fee-based businesses, and economically vibrant markets throughout our footprint all contributed to our third quarter results. Total revenue increased 3 percent on a reported basis and 2 percent on an adjusted basis (1) compared to the second quarter of 2026. Net interest income increased 2 percent driven primarily by fixed-rate asset turnover, average loan growth, higher hedging income, credit interest recoveries, one additional day in the quarter and continued prudent management of deposit costs, partially offset by an increase in non-deposit funding costs. Net interest margin increased 2 basis points to 3.68 percent. 2 Non-interest income increased 7 percent on a reported basis and 3 percent on an adjusted basis (1) during the third quarter . With respect to adjusted items, the company incurred $15 million in securities losses in the third quarter compared to $40 million in the second quarter, attributable to the execution of additional securities repositioning trades. Record capital markets income increased 27 percent driven by higher mergers and acquisitions advisory revenue, securities underwriting and placement fees, commercial swap income and syndication revenue. Service charges increased 2 percent reflecting record Treasury Management income, one additional business day in the quarter, and seasonally higher consumer-related activity. Commercial credit fee income increased 25 percent driven by higher standby letter of credit income and commercial unused fees. Bank-owned life insurance increased 33 percent due to higher death benefit proceeds recognized during the quarter. Wealth management income decreased 3 percent following a record second quarter, primarily reflecting lower production volumes. Market value adjustments associated with employee benefit assets declined $28 million during the quarter and were largely offset by corresponding changes in non-interest expense. reference.summary: Regions Financial Corporation, a financial holding company, provides various banking and related products and services to individual and corporate customers. It operates through three segments: Corporate Bank, Consumer Bank, and Wealth Management. The Corporate Bank segment offers commercial banking services, such as commercial and industrial, commercial real estate, and investor real estate lending; equipment lease financing; deposit products; capital markets activities, such as securities underwriting and placement; and loan syndication and placement, foreign exchange, derivatives, merger and acquisition, and other advisory services to corporate, middle market, and commercial real estate developers and investors.
